land.text: Richard the Justiciar's ducatus: Autunais, Beaunois, Auxerrois, Nivernais, Chaunois and Massois

predecessors.note: The page names the Kingdom of the Burgundians as predecessor; the land of Autun, Nevers and Auxerre was part of West Francia (Richard asked Carloman II to recognise him as count of Autun in 880).

land.text: the Duchy of Burgundy and Picardy, annexed in 1477 and recognised at Arras on 23 December 1482

successors.note: Franche-Comté and Artois stayed French as Margaret's dowry until the Treaty of Senlis (1493).

land.text: the Burgundian Netherlands, which passed to Maximilian and Mary's son Philip

successors.note: Cliopatria's House of Habsburg row (1482-1486) is the same land; the dedicated Habsburg Netherlands dossier is the successor state.

The page gives no area. correction.text: the ducal lands west of the Saône: Côte-d'Or, Saône-et-Loire and part of the Yonne, carried forward from the 1010 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Duchy of Burgundy row 1018-1384 and draws the land inside the Kingdom of Arles (71-77 of the 137 cells of the gazetteer's Burgundy region, Dijon included, in 1100-1350) although the duchy was a French fief ('Future dukes were to owe allegiance only to the crown of France', 1032). The French article gives the duchy as roughly the modern Côte-d'Or, Saône-et-Loire and part of the Yonne, with vassal counties held 'de manière discontinue'; the 1010 shape (Côte-d'Or 95%, Saône-et-Loire 66%, Yonne 21%) is carried forward. No page opened dates a boundary change in these centuries (page silent), so this is a bridge; Nevers, Auxerre, Tonnerre and the Franche-Comté stay outside it. [Repair 2026-10-25: ends 1361 (the duchy reverts to the crown, ledger loss December 1361); 1362 has no keyframe because the land is the king's; the shape resumes in the 1363 keyframe. One dated change inside the bridge: Hugh IV gave up the barony the page calls 'Salon' for the counties of Chalon and Auxonne in 1237 (ledger gain; both lie inside the carried shape, so it does not change the outline). Odo IV and Joan held Artois and the Free County from 1330 in personal union (Odo IV page); they are other states and are not drawn here. The Capetian dukes' years 1076-1349 are now in the ruler strip.]

region.text: Richard's ducatus: 'the regions of Autunais, Beaunois', Auxerrois, Nivernais, Chaunois and Massois

ledger.note: 918: Richard the Justiciar is titled Duke of Burgundy. 'by 918 count Richard was titled as Duke of Burgundy' (infobox 'Established: c. 918'); the French article: 'Vers 918, il est titré dux, donc premier duc de Bourgogne' and he 'réunit alors les comtés d'Autun, de Nevers et d'Auxerre'. The year is the page's (approximate); the land is the page's list of the ducatus read as the gazetteer's Burgundy region.

region.text: the County of Nevers: 'Around 990, Landry was granted the County of Nevers by his father-in-law Count Otto-William of Burgundy'

ledger.note: 989: Nevers leaves the ducal ducatus as Landry's county. Landry page: 'Landry was the first hereditary Count of Nevers from 989 to 1028'; 'Around 990, Landry was granted the County of Nevers by his father-in-law Count Otto-William of Burgundy', 'with the consent of Duke Henry I of Burgundy and King Hugh Capet of France'. The year is the page's opening line (the grant itself is 'around 990'); the region (the Nièvre, 27 cells of the 1003 shape) is my reading of the Nivernais. Mirrors county-of-nevers /ledger/0 (found, counterpart duchy-of-burgundy), which draws the same Nièvre from 989; the earlier version of this dossier kept it in the duchy to 1009. [Repair 2026-10-25: option (b) of the review, so the county-of-nevers dossier needs no change.]

region.text: the duchy's lands west of the Saône, fought over by the crown and Otto-William's party

ledger.note: 1003: King Robert II's war for the duchy opens at Auxerre. Henry I of Burgundy died 15 October 1002 without a legitimate heir; in 1003 Robert's armed intervention, with Norman troops, failed in front of Auxerre and Saint-Germain d'Auxerre, in a rivalry over Auxerre between Bishop Hugh of Chalon and Count Landry of Nevers, Otto-William's son-in-law; in 1004 Robert besieged Beaune (the page's account, paraphrased).

union.text: Auxerre and Avallon, given up by Landry
the ducal lands taken by Robert

region.text: the duchy west of the Saône

ledger.note: 1005: Otto-William gives up the duchy; Robert holds it for the crown. In 1005 Robert took Avallon and then Auxerre and Landry was reconciled by giving up the counties of Avallon and Auxerre; in 1005-1006 Otto-William renounced the ducal title and his stepfather's possessions reverted to the Crown, except Dijon (the page's account, paraphrased). The French article also says 'C'est finalement Robert qui l'emporte en 1005'. The Auxerre page lists Landry as count of Auxerre 1002-1028 and Cliopatria keeps Auxerre in Nevers from 1010: the pages disagree about who held Auxerre afterwards; the duchy's loss of the Auxerrois is the 1005 loss recorded below.

region.text: the counties of Avallon and Auxerre: 'Count Landry was reconciled with the King by renouncing the Counties of Avallon and Auxerre'

ledger.note: 1005: Landry gives up Auxerre and Avallon and the Auxerrois leaves the duke's shape. Robert II page: 'They took Avallon after a few days of fighting, then Auxerre'; 'Count Landry was reconciled with the King by renouncing the Counties of Avallon and Auxerre' (the page does not say to whom the counties went; read here as the crown, which also held the duchy 1005-1016). The region is the 36 cells (about 9,100 km2, 2.4-3.7 E, 47.1-48.3 N, round Auxerre) that drop out between Cliopatria's 1003 and 1010 shapes once the Nièvre (989) is taken out, so it explains the 1003 to 1010 fall from 31,613 to 18,169 km2 together with the 989 loss. The Auxerre page lists Landerich of Monceau as count of Auxerre 1002-1028 and Cliopatria draws Auxerre in Nevers from 1010: the pages disagree about the holder afterwards. kingdom-of-france has no 1005 event (mirror needed). [Repair 2026-10-25]

region.text: Dijon and its county

ledger.note: 1016: Dijon passes to the crown and Robert II takes full possession of the duchy. Bishop Brunon of Roucy (who held Dijon) died on 30 January 1016; Robert installed Lambert de Vignory as bishop of Langres, who ceded Dijon and its county to the King (paraphrase); 'Robert II finally entered into full possession of the Duchy of Burgundy.' The French article: 'Il octroie en 1016 le duché à son deuxième fils Henri'. [Repair 2026-10-25: the counterpart is the episcopal lordship of Langres, which is no state and has no dossier. Dijon (5.04 E, 47.32 N) lies inside the 1010 shape and the 1005-1017 keyframes, so the event is a caption for the end of the succession war and moves no outline.]

1032: the duchy passes to the Capetian House of Burgundy. King Henry I 'later ceded it as an appanage to his younger brother Robert in 1032'; 'Robert became the ancestor of the ducal House of Burgundy, a cadet branch of the royal Capet dynasty' and 'Future dukes were to owe allegiance only to the crown of France'. Robert II page: Robert was named heir in 1030 and installed in 1032; the French article dates his accession as duke to 1025.

region.text: the counties of Chalon and Auxonne, taken in exchange for the barony the page calls Salon

ledger.note: 1237: Hugh IV acquires the counties of Chalon and Auxonne. Hugh IV page: he 'gave up the barony of Salon for the counties of Chalon and Auxonne in 1237' (an exchange with John l'Antique de Chalon). Both places lie inside the carried 1010 shape (Chalon-sur-Saône 4.85 E 46.78 N, Auxonne 5.38 E 47.19 N), so the 1018-1361 keyframe does not change; the barony the page spells 'Salon' (Salins, in Franche-Comté, in other accounts) is not in the shape. The only dated boundary event the pages give for the 1018-1384 bridge. [Repair 2026-10-25]

region.text: the duchy: 'the duchy reverted to King John II of France and the royal House of Valois'

ledger.note: 1361: the last Capetian duke, Philip of Rouvres, dies and the duchy reverts to the crown. 'the duchy reverted to King John II of France' (1361); 'On 28 December 1361, he received the homage of the Burgundian nobility'; letters patent merging it into the crown were scrapped when the Estates refused. Mirrors kingdom-of-france /ledger/43 and royal-domain-of-france /ledger/30 (gain 1361). Replaces the former rename. The dynasty changes from the Capetian House of Burgundy to the Valois. [Repair 2026-10-25]

region.text: the duchy: 'King John II ceded the duchy to his younger son Philip'

ledger.note: 1363: John II gives the duchy to his son Philip the Bold, founding the Valois dukes of Burgundy. 'King John II ceded the duchy to his younger son Philip' (1363): 'The king secretly created him duke on 6 September 1363.' Charles V confirmed the title on 2 June 1364. kingdom-of-france /ledger/45 and royal-domain-of-france /ledger/31 date their loss to 1364 and should say 1363 (the 1364 date is the confirmation). Replaces the former rename. [Repair 2026-10-25]

region.text: Flanders, Artois, Antwerp and Mechelen

ledger.note: 1384: Philip the Bold inherits Flanders and Artois. Philip took office 'as count and lord of Antwerp, Artois, Flanders, Mechelen, and Rethel in 1384', 'upon the death of Count Louis II of Flanders in 1384', through his wife Margaret III.

region.text: the County of Burgundy (Franche-Comté), an Imperial fief

ledger.note: 1384: the Franche-Comté joins the duke's lands in personal union. The page's table lists 'Franche-Comté' under the 1384 inheritance row; the text calls it 'the County of Burgundy (Franche-Comté) east of it, an Imperial fief'.

region.text: the counties of Nevers and Rethel (Auxerre cells of the Nevers shape excluded)

ledger.note: 1384: Nevers and Rethel come with the Flanders inheritance. 'Cet héritage est réalisé en 1384' for Flanders, the County of Burgundy and 'des comtés de Nevers et de Rethel (fiefs français)'. The Nevers row is drawn inside the duke's shape from 1385 (Cliopatria). [Repair 2026-10-25: the 30 km disc round Auxerre is cut out of the Nevers shape, because the Auxerre page has the county sold to the king in 1370 and Burgundy's only from 1435.]

region.text: the county of Charolais, sold by Bernard VII of Armagnac

ledger.note: 1390: Philip the Bold buys the county of Charolais. 'John's grandson Count Bernard VII of Armagnac sold the county to Duke Philip II of Burgundy in 1390.' (the Armagnac page: Jean III alienated it in 1390; the Bernard VII page has Bernard succeed in 1391, so the pages disagree on the seller). Mirrors county-of-armagnac /ledger/10. The 1395 Cliopatria shape holds all 8 cells of a 25 km disc round Charolles, the 1385 shape 5; the keyframes add the disc from 1390. The Philip the Good page has the county as an appanage of Philip from 28 January 1405. The gazetteer has no Charolais region yet, so the region is a 25 km disc round Charolles (46.43 N 4.28 E). [Repair 2026-10-25]

region.text: Nevers with Rethel (Auxerre cells of the Nevers shape excluded)

ledger.note: 1407: Nevers and Rethel pass to Philip the Bold's younger son Philip II. 'both held by Philip's younger son Philip II from 1407'. The Philip II page's infobox gives Nevers from 1404 and Rethel from 1406; Cliopatria draws the split in 1407 and the ledger follows it. [Repair 2026-10-25: Auxerre excluded as in the 1384 gain.]

region.text: the County of Hainaut, administered by Philip for Jacqueline

ledger.note: 3 July 1428: the Treaty of Delft puts Hainaut in Philip's hands. 'Jacqueline kept her titles of Countess of Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut', 'the administration of her territories was placed in the hands of Philip', 'who was also appointed as her heir in case she died without children'. The treaty covered Holland and Zeeland too, but county-of-holland has no occupation event, so only Hainaut is recorded (eu-09 can add the Holland side). Mirrors county-of-hainaut /ledger/6. [Repair 2026-10-25]

region.text: the County of Namur

ledger.note: 1429: the duke takes possession of Namur. 'acheté au marquis de Namur Jean III pour 132 000 couronnes d'or en 1421' and 'En 1429, celui-ci prend possession du comté de Namur'. The Burgundian Netherlands page: 'Philip the Good purchased the County of Namur in 1421'.

region.text: the Duchy of Brabant (and Limburg)

ledger.note: 1430: Philip the Good inherits Brabant and Limburg. 'inherited the Duchies of Brabant and Limburg in 1430'; 'Philip of Brabant died childless, leaving his cousin Philip as his heir'. Limburg has no separate gazetteer region and is read inside the Brabant shape.

region.text: the County of Hainaut

ledger.note: 1432: Philip's administration of Hainaut becomes possession. 'seized the Counties of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland in 1432' (Burgundian Netherlands); the Jacqueline page has Jacqueline sign over all her lands 'At Easter 1433' (her reign ends 12 April 1433 in its infobox) and its Hainaut succession box ends 1432, so the pages disagree by one year. Mirrors county-of-hainaut /ledger/7 (1432). [Repair 2026-10-25]

region.text: the County of Hainaut

ledger.note: 1432: Hainaut falls to the duke. 'seized the Counties of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland in 1432' (the French article: 'seront ajoutés aux possessions bourguignonnes en 1433').

region.text: the Counties of Holland and Zeeland

ledger.note: 1432: Holland and Zeeland fall to the duke ('seized the Counties of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland in 1432'; the table: 'Offered position after victory of the Hollandic cities in the Hook and Cod wars'). Cliopatria draws them from 1450.

region.text: The County of Auxerre

ledger.note: 1435: the county of Auxerre passes to the duke. Treaty of Arras, 20/21 September 1435: the page's lead-in 'the following domains became vassal states of the Duke of Burgundy' lists 'The County of Auxerre and the County of Boulogne'; 'Philip the Good was exempted from rendering homage, fealty, or service to Charles VII'. Auxerre page: 'Count John IV sold it to the King of France in 1370' and, 'After the Treaty of Arras (1435)', it 'returned once again' to Burgundy, so in 1435 it was crown land and the gain is from kingdom-of-france (royal-domain-of-france /ledger/43 records the loss, 30 km disc). The page's 'vassal' wording is the duke's suzerainty; the French article has Charles VII 'cède' it. Replaces the vassal_start that named a county of Auxerre which no longer existed. [Repair 2026-10-25]

region.text: The Somme towns and Péronne

ledger.note: 1435: the Somme towns and Péronne pass to the duke. Treaty of Arras, 20/21 September 1435: the page's lead-in 'the following domains became vassal states of the Duke of Burgundy' lists 'The Somme towns and Péronne'; 'Philip the Good was exempted from rendering homage, fealty, or service to Charles VII'. The French article: 'Charles VII cède à Philippe le Bon les villes de la Somme'. The region is the Somme department minus a 35 km disc round Abbeville (Ponthieu is a separate item, below). Mirrors royal-domain-of-france /ledger/43. Cliopatria draws them in the duke's shape from 1440. The redemption by Louis XI (400,000 écus, undated on every page opened) is not recorded: see the notes. [Repair 2026-10-25: split from the former Ponthieu vassal_start]

region.text: The Vermandois, with its capital Saint-Quentin.

ledger.note: 1435: the Vermandois with Saint-Quentin passes to the duke. Treaty of Arras, 20/21 September 1435: the page's lead-in 'the following domains became vassal states of the Duke of Burgundy' lists 'The Vermandois, with its capital Saint-Quentin.'; 'Philip the Good was exempted from rendering homage, fealty, or service to Charles VII'. The region is a 25 km disc round Saint-Quentin (49.85 N 3.29 E), not Cliopatria's 1210 County of Vermandois shape (19,510 km2), because that county ended in 1213 and the land was the crown's (royal-domain-of-france /ledger/43). [Repair 2026-10-25]

region.text: le comté de Mâcon and la vicomté de Bar-sur-Seine

ledger.note: 1435: Mâcon and Bar-sur-Seine pass to the duke. French article: « Charles VII cède à Philippe le Bon les villes de la Somme, le comté de Mâcon », « la vicomté de Bar-sur-Seine et le comté d'Auxerre » (the English page does not name Mâcon or Bar-sur-Seine; the year and month are the treaty's). Confidence 2: the year is the treaty's, the discs (25 km at Mâcon, 15 km at Bar-sur-Seine) are my reading. Mâcon is already in Cliopatria's shape from 1385. [Repair 2026-10-25: new, from the review's thin note]

region.text: Ponthieu

ledger.note: 1435: Ponthieu becomes the duke's vassal. Treaty of Arras, 20/21 September 1435: the page's lead-in 'the following domains became vassal states of the Duke of Burgundy' lists 'Ponthieu'; 'Philip the Good was exempted from rendering homage, fealty, or service to Charles VII'. county-of-ponthieu /ledger/6 quotes the Ponthieu page for the same exchange ('possession of Ponthieu'); that page was not reopened here. The region is a 35 km disc round Abbeville. county-of-ponthieu records only a rename in 1435 and 1477, so its owner must add vassal_start 1435 / vassal_end 1477 (counterpart duchy-of-burgundy); royal-domain-of-france /ledger/43 also takes Ponthieu out of the domain as a loss to burgundian-state. [Repair 2026-10-25: split from the Somme towns]

region.text: The County of Boulogne

ledger.note: 1435: the county of Boulogne becomes the duke's vassal. Treaty of Arras, 20/21 September 1435: the page's lead-in 'the following domains became vassal states of the Duke of Burgundy' lists 'The County of Auxerre and the County of Boulogne'; 'Philip the Good was exempted from rendering homage, fealty, or service to Charles VII'. The vassal is the count of Auvergne, who held Boulogne since 1259-1260 (county-of-boulogne /ledger/6 merges it into county-of-auvergne; county-of-boulogne is dormant 1259-1477), so the counterpart is county-of-auvergne, whose owner (eu-10) must add vassal_start 1435 / vassal_end 1477 for the Boulogne polygon (506 km2). Kept as a vassal, not a gain, because county-of-auvergne keeps Boulogne to its 1477 loss to Louis XI and the page says only 'vassal states'. [Repair 2026-10-25: the review's second option]

region.text: the Duchy of Luxembourg

ledger.note: 1443: Luxembourg passes to the duke. 'and the Duchy of Luxembourg in 1443' (table: 'Conquest'); the French article: bought in 1441, controlled from 1443 ('ne contrôle le duché qu'à partir de 1443'). Cliopatria draws it from 1450.

region.text: Sigismund's pawned possessions in Upper Alsace

ledger.note: 1469: Sigismund of Austria pawns his Alsace lands to Charles the Bold. 'Initially in 1469, Duke Sigismund of Habsburg of Austria pawned his possessions in the Alsace' (Treaty of Saint-Omer, 50,000 florins). Charles page: on 21 March 1469 he received Sigismund 'to negotiate the purchase of Sigismund's lands in Upper Alsace'; his rights were limited because most land rights were mortgaged. Cliopatria does not draw Alsace in any shape of the duchy.

region.text: the Duchy of Lorraine as a Burgundian protectorate

ledger.note: 1473: Lorraine becomes a Burgundian protectorate. 'In 1473, through negotiations with the new Duke of Lorraine, René II, Charles secured the right to move his armies through Lorraine and place Burgundian captains in its important fortifications, effectively turning the duchy into a Burgundian protectorate.'

region.text: the Duchy of Guelders

ledger.note: 1473: Charles the Bold conquers Guelders. Duke Arnold died in February 1473 and 'bequeathed the duchy to Charles'; 'On 9 June 1473, he entered Maastricht with a sizeable army'; Roermond and Venlo surrendered and Nijmegen resisted. The Burgundian Netherlands page: 'in 1473 annexed the Duchy of Guelders, which had been pawned by late Arnold of Egmond'.

region.text: Sigismund's pawned possessions in Upper Alsace

ledger.note: 1474: Burgundian rule in Alsace collapses. Charles's deputy Peter von Hagenbach was later overthrown and executed by the League of Constance in 1474 (Charles page, paraphrased; the Burgundian Wars page: executed shortly after the 1474 Konstanz accord); the page gives no later Burgundian hold on the pledged lands.

region.text: the Duchy of Lorraine

ledger.note: 30 November 1475: Charles the Bold invades Lorraine and the protectorate ends in conquest. René II page: 'Charles invaded the duchy and René was forced to quit Nancy (30 November 1475)'; the Charles page: 'Splitting his army into two, he advanced through Lorraine without resistance and captured Nancy'. Matches duchy-of-lorraine (November 1475). [Repair 2026-10-25: dated, was confidence 1 and 1475 bridged from the shape]

region.text: the Duchy of Lorraine, held without annexation

ledger.note: 30 November 1475: Charles occupies Lorraine, taking Nancy. 'Charles invaded the duchy and René was forced to quit Nancy (30 November 1475)' (René II page); the Duchy of Lorraine page says the duchy was 'briefly occupied by the dukes of Burgundy and the kings of France' without a date. Mirrors duchy-of-lorraine's occupation_start (1475-11). [Repair 2026-10-25]

region.text: the Duchy of Lorraine

ledger.note: 5 October 1476: René II retakes Nancy and the occupation of Lorraine ends. 'He regained the city on 5 October the following year' (René II page; the Charles page gives '6 October' without a year); the Battle of Nancy page has the siege from 22 October 1476 and the battle on 5 January 1477. [Repair 2026-10-25: day and year now on the page]

region.text: the Duchy of Guelders

ledger.note: 1477: Guelders breaks away after Charles's death at Nancy (5 January 1477). 'Charles's former conquests, Liège and Guelders, quickly sought independence'; the War of the Burgundian Succession page: by 1492-93 Guelders was independent under Charles II of Egmont.

region.text: the County of Boulogne

ledger.note: 1477: Boulogne leaves the duke's vassalage. 'almost all of the aforementioned territories (except Flanders) were successfully seized by French forces' in the first months of 1477; the page names Artois, Boulogne, Ponthieu and Vermandois. The vassal is the count of Auvergne (see the 1435 vassal_start); county-of-auvergne /ledger/7 and royal-domain-of-france /ledger/49 (1478) take Boulogne to the crown.

region.text: Ponthieu

ledger.note: 1477: Ponthieu leaves the duke's vassalage. 'almost all of the aforementioned territories (except Flanders) were successfully seized by French forces' in the first months of 1477; the page names Artois, Boulogne, Ponthieu and Vermandois (the Ponthieu page: 'In 1477 Ponthieu was reconquered by King Louis XI of France'). Mirrors county-of-ponthieu /ledger/7-8 (crown land from 1477). [Repair 2026-10-25: Ponthieu only; the Somme towns follow the duchy and Picardy to the Treaty of Arras]

region.text: the Duchy of Burgundy and Picardy, 'seized by French forces' with the 1435 domains (Auxerre, the Somme towns, Saint-Quentin, Mâcon, Bar-sur-Seine)

ledger.note: January 1477: Louis XI occupies the duchy and Picardy; the duke's heirs keep the claim. 'Already on 29 January, the assembly of the Duchy of Burgundy acknowledged the full reincorporation into the French realm'; 'almost all of the aforementioned territories (except Flanders) were successfully seized by French forces' in the first months of 1477; the Duchy page: Louis XI 'declared the duchy escheated'; the French article: 'L'armée française occupe dès janvier 1477 le duché de Bourgogne'. Mirrors kingdom-of-france /ledger/64 (occupation_start, Burgundy and Picardy); the formal annexation is the Treaty of Arras (December 1482). The Ponthieu disc is left out because Ponthieu is already crown land (vassal_end above). The 1435 domains lie inside this occupation; they are not given a separate 1477 loss, because burgundian-state /ledger/20 and royal-domain-of-france /ledger/53 date their return to 1482. [Repair 2026-10-25: was a contest_start; the contest is kept only for Franche-Comté, Artois and the Charolais]

region.text: Franche-Comté, Artois and the Charolais, taken or claimed by French forces from 1477

ledger.note: 1477: Franche-Comté, Artois and the Charolais are fought over with France. 'almost all of the aforementioned territories (except Flanders) were successfully seized by French forces' (Artois named); Franche-Comté was occupied by French soldiers in early 1477 (Burgundian Wars page); 'the county was seized by King Louis XI' and 'Charolais rebelled in support of Mary of Burgundy' the same year (County of Charolais page). Maximilian and Mary contest them until 1482; house-of-habsburg records the same contest. [Repair 2026-10-25]

region.text: the Duchy of Burgundy and Picardy

ledger.note: 23 December 1482: the French occupation ends in annexation. 'Maximilian recognized the French annexation of the Duchy of Burgundy and several other territories' (Second Treaty of Arras); the Duchy page has him recognise the annexation of the Duchy and County of Burgundy. Mirrors kingdom-of-france /ledger/68 (1482). [Repair 2026-10-25]

region.text: the Duchy of Burgundy and Picardy, with the 1435 domains Auxerre, the Somme towns, Saint-Quentin, Mâcon and Bar-sur-Seine

ledger.note: 23 December 1482: the Treaty of Arras gives the duchy and Picardy to France. 'Maximilian recognized the French annexation of the Duchy of Burgundy and several other territories' (the Duchy page: 'Maximilian recognised the annexation of the Duchy and County of Burgundy'); Senlis (1493): 'the Duchy of Burgundy and Picardy were lost definitively to France'. [Repair 2026-10-25: the region names the 1435 gains explicitly (Auxerre, Mâcon, Bar-sur-Seine and the Somme towns lie in or beside the two regions); this is their matching loss to kingdom-of-france, after the 1477-1482 occupation. Mirrors kingdom-of-france /ledger/69.]

region.text: Franche-Comté, Artois and the Charolais, Margaret's dowry

ledger.note: 23 December 1482: Franche-Comté and Artois are treated as the dowry of Margaret of Austria and stay French until the Treaty of Senlis (1493). 'Regarding the Free County of Burgundy (Franche-Comté) and County of Artois, they were treated as Margaret's dowry'; Burgundian Netherlands page: 'France retained Artois'. The Burgundian Wars page says the Peace of Zürich (24 January 1478) returned Franche-Comté to Maximilian for 150,000 guilders; the pages do not reconcile the two. [Repair 2026-10-25: the Charolais added: 'by the Treaty of Senlis (1493) Charolais was returned to the Habsburg dynasty' (County of Charolais page).]

region.text: the zone fought over 1477-1482

ledger.note: 23 December 1482: the War of the Burgundian Succession ends with the Second Treaty of Arras (infobox 1477-1482). 'France agreed to return the affluent County of Flanders, which passed to Maximilian.' and 'Maximilian recognized the French annexation of the Duchy of Burgundy and several other territories.'

region.text: the Burgundian Netherlands left to Maximilian

ledger.note: 1482: the Burgundian state ends and its Netherlands pass to the Habsburgs. The infobox gives Disestablished 1482, and Maximilian gained Flanders 'according to the 1482 Treaty of Arras after his wife Mary had suddenly died, while France retained Artois.' War of the Burgundian Succession page: 'In 1482, Mary died and her four-year-old son' succeeded her. Cliopatria's row ends 1481 and the Habsburg row takes the Netherlands in 1482.

wars.name: Succession war for the Duchy of Burgundy
wars.outcome: Robert II won in 1005 (Landry reconciled, Otto-William renounced) and took full possession in 1016 when Dijon was ceded; Henry received the ducal title and Robert I the duchy in 1032.
wars.note: Fighting 1003-1005 (Auxerre, Beaune, Avallon); the French article calls it a war between Robert II and Otte-Guillaume that Robert won in 1005.

wars.name: Burgundian conquest of Guelders
wars.outcome: Charles marched into Guelders in 1471 as mediator; Arnold died in February 1473 and bequeathed the duchy to Charles, who took it in June 1473 (Maastricht 9 June, Nijmegen after resistance). It broke away after Charles's death in 1477.

wars.name: Burgundian Wars
wars.outcome: 'Lorrain-Swiss victory': defeats at Grandson (1476) and Morat (1476) and Charles's death at Nancy on 5 January 1477; 'Extinction of Valois Burgundy and division between Valois France and Habsburg heirs'.

wars.name: War of the Burgundian Succession

zones.text: the duchy, Franche-Comté, Artois and Picardy

wars.outcome: France kept the Duchy of Burgundy and Picardy; Maximilian regained Flanders; Franche-Comté and Artois were Margaret's dowry and were returned only at Senlis in 1493.
wars.note: French defeat at Guinegate, 7 August 1479; Auxois, Charolais and Beaune rebelled in 1478 and surrendered in 1479.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary for the duchy before 1385; the county lists are approximate.
The Treaties of Arras (1435, 1482) name the lands exchanged but fix no surveyed line; the duke's possessions are scattered fiefs.

notes:
Written for eu-10-e from nine pages (the page budget); repaired 2026-10-25 after review (twenty-five more pages, listed in sources). Cliopatria's row has two lives, 1003-1017 and 1385-1481. 1018-1384 is drawn as the Kingdom of Arles (71-77 of 137 Burgundy-region cells, Dijon included, 1100-1350): this dossier carries the duchy through those centuries as a new keyframe (bridged from the 1010 shape; the only dated event inside it is Hugh IV's exchange of 1237 (Chalon and Auxonne); the keyframe is cut in 1362 while the king holds the duchy). The first duke (c. 918) is added as keyframes 918-988 and 989-1002 over the West Franks row; the Nièvre is Nevers' from 989, the Auxerrois leaves in 1005. The row's 1385-1481 shapes are the whole Valois composite, which eu-10-x also wrote as burgundian-state (1363-1482, predecessor this slug); the compile must decide which to draw. This dossier is the Cliopatria row and ends with it, in December 1482.
PAGES DISAGREE: the duchy was annexed in January 1477 (assembly of 29 January; French occupation) while the state is dated to 1482, so 1477-1482 is an occupation of the duchy and Picardy and a contest for Franche-Comté, Artois and the Charolais.
